analysis:
The PR changes one documentation line in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (line 52 on the head side). It rewords the video-input description from inline data:video/mp4 or data:video/quicktime URLs to inline base64 MP4 or QuickTime URLs, constant or variable frame rate, with the allowed labels defined in MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders. No code, config, authorization, attestation, encryption, or key-handling behavior changes. The supplied units (base lines 822-1671) do not contain the changed line itself. They were reviewed as surrounding context and show no security-relevant change.

Threat-model relevance: T-050 (inline video plaintext exposed through provider temp files) and A-001 (consumer prompts) are the nearest entries. The wording suggests variable-frame-rate video is now admitted, but this PR contains no media-ingest source. Any real change in MediaIngest, such as new decoder paths, size or duration bounds, or temp-file handling, is not visible here and was not evaluated.

Open question for integration: if a companion code change in this PR broadens the admitted video formats, check that the T-050 mitigations (no plaintext temp files, bounded decode) still hold. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression.

The rest of the base context describes existing CLI, fan helper, logout, update, and report behavior, and I identified no new attack surface in it.
